chains.title: TCF7L2 loss-of-binding at the 8q24 pELS

links.claim: TCF7L2 is the stronger HCT116-occupied candidate at this base: ENCODE TCF7L2 ChIP-seq has peaks containing the variant in HCT116 (E05). The ref T allele is predicted to bind more than alt C, but this is low-confidence: TCF7L2 has no own QBiC-SELEX model, and E20 reports only a CIS-BP-mapped TCF7 model at weak k-mers, so the mapped model is not direct TCF7L2 allelic evidence. Occupancy supports TCF7L2 at the element, not allele-specific binding at the base.

The variant lies in cCRE EH38E3858447, a pELS, and TCF7L2 ChIP-seq contains the variant in HCT116. The cCRE activity z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, so HCT116-specific enhancer activity is only partly supported.

POU5F1B is the closest protein-coding gene with local L2G support at 79.1 kb from its TSS, but the L2G credible sets are PSA and urinary incontinence, not colorectal cancer, and no colorectal eQTL is provided; MYC remains a farther long-range alternative.
HCT116 is a colorectal cancer cell line that expresses TCF7L2 at 63.61 TPM and has TCF7L2 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant.

TCF7L2-dependent enhancer activity at 8q24 is a plausible colorectal cancer mechanism, but this exact variant has no GWAS Catalog association, no significant GTEx eQTL, and only general POU5F1B/colorectal cancer literature plus Open Targets gene-disease support.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr8:127401265:T>C, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000971), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 40 occupied (6 with a strong site), 5 of 103 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 11 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 517 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 5 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
